en: *Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa*,
*Dhammānuloma* (1), *Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi* (1), 1.22.
The Triplet on Internal Objects (*Ajjhattārammaṇattika*).
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.
Dependent on a state with an internal object, there arises a state with an internal object by way of the root condition—[namely,] a state with an internal object...
Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates arise … two aggregates … At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one internal object aggregate,
three aggregates arise … two aggregates … Dependent on a state with an external object,
a state with an external object arises by way of root condition: [dependent on] an external object …
Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates [arise] …pe… dependent on two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one external-object aggregate,
three aggregates [arise] …pe… dependent on two aggregates …pe….
Object, etc.
Dependent on a state with an internal object, a state with an internal object arises by way of object-condition … [and so on] … by way of non-disappearance condition. (Abbreviated.
Section on Enumeration:
Pure.

With root condition, there are two [results] in the object condition (*ārammaṇa*)—[abbreviated; in all cases there are two]—and two in the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*). (Thus it should be counted.
Positive Order (*anuloma*).
1.22.1.2. Negative Order of Conditions (*paccayapaccanīya*).
Section on Analysis:
Not-root Condition.
Dependent on a state with an internal object, there arises a state with an internal object by way of the not-root condition: [dependent on] a rootless [state].
In dependence on one aggregate with an internal object, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates … At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking,
in dependence on one aggregate with an internal object, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates … In dependence on aggregates accompanied by doubt or accompanied by restlessness,
delusion accompanied by doubt or accompanied by restlessness [arises].
Dependent on a state with an external object, a state with an external object arises by way of the not-root condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate with an external object,

three aggregates arise … two aggregates … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … dependent on doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates, doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied delusion arises.
Not by way of predominance, etc.:

dependent on a state with internal object, a state with internal object arises by way of not-predominance condition … (similar to the positive conascence [condition], with no difference). By way of not-prenascence condition: in the immaterial plane, [dependent on] a state with internal object…
In dependence on one aggregate … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe ….
In dependence on a state with an external object, a state with an external object arises by way of not-prenascence condition:
in the immaterial plane, in dependence on one aggregate with an external object, three aggregates arise … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … [by way of] not-postnascence condition.
… not by way of repetition-condition … (as in the case of co-nascence) … not by way of kamma-condition:

dependent on internal objects, aggregates, arises volition with internal objects. Dependent on a state with external objects, there arises a state with external objects by way of kamma-condition: dependent on aggregates with external objects, arises volition with external objects.

Dependent on a state with internal object, a state with internal object arises by way of non-resultant condition (*navipāka-paccaya*) (there is no rebirth-linking here) … by way of non-jhāna condition …pe… one [consciousness] accompanied by the fivefold sense-consciousness with internal object …pe….
Dependent on a state with external object, a state with external object arises by way of non-jhāna condition— one [consciousness] accompanied by the fivefold sense-consciousness.
In dependence on one aggregate with an external object, three aggregates [arise] … [and so on] … by way of not-path condition … by way of non-dissociation condition—
in the formless realm, in dependence on one internal-objective aggregate,

three aggregates [arise] … [and so on] …. In dependence on a state with an external object, a state with an external object arises by way of non-dissociation condition— in the formless realm, in dependence on one aggregate with an external object, three aggregates [arise] … [and so on] ….
In the Enumeration Chapter, under the Pure [condition],

there are two for not-root, two for not-predominance, two for not-prenascence, two for not-postnascence, two for not-repetition, two for not-kamma, two for not-resultant, two for not-jhāna, two for not-path, and two for not-dissociation. (Thus it should be counted.)
The Negative (Paccanīya). 1.22.1.3.
Positive-Negative Conditions (Paccayānulomapaccanīya):

With root condition (hetupaccaya), there are two [instances] for non-predominance (na-adhipati) …pe… two for non-resultant (na-vipāka), and two for non-dissociation (na-vippayutta). (It should be counted in this manner.)
Positive-Negative. 1.22.1.4. Negative-Positive Conditionality:
With non-root condition, there are two for object; two for proximity; two for contiguity … pe … two for path … pe … two for non-disappearance. (It should be counted in this manner.)
Negative-Positive (Paccanīyānuloma).
Chapter on Dependence (Paṭiccasamuppādavāra). 1.22.2–6. Section on Co-nascence Condition, Support, Conjoined, and Associated (Sahajāta-paccaya-nissaya-saṃsaṭṭha-sampayuttavāra).
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, dependence, association, and conjunction are similar to the section on "dependent" [paṭicca]). 1.22.7.
Chapter of Questions (Pañhāvāra) 1.22.7.1.
Positive Conditionality (Paccayānuloma)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition. A state with an internal object is a condition, by way of root condition, for a state with an internal object—namely, those states with an internal object.

Roots that have internal objects are related to their associated aggregates by way of root condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots with internal objects are related to their associated aggregates by way of root condition.

A state with external objects is related to a state with external objects by way of root condition: roots with external objects are related to their associated aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe ….
Object Condition:
A state with an internal object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with an internal object.
[One] reviews the internal base of infinite consciousness; one reviews the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; [one reviews] that which has an internal object.

One reviews the divine eye internally, the divine ear element … [and so on] … the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power … [and so on] … the knowledge of recollecting past lives … [and so on] … the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their karma … [and so on] … one reviews the knowledge of future states.
Noble ones review defilements that have been abandoned within themselves; they review defilements that have been suppressed.
They know the defilements previously practiced. One practices insight into internal aggregates with an internal object as impermanent ...
[as before] ... one relishes and delights in them; taking that as an object, lust with an internal object arises ...
[as before] ... grief arises. Internal aggregates with an internal object are the objects of the knowledge of recollection of past lives.
Knowledge of the destination according to kamma, knowledge of the future, and adverting are related to [their respective objects] by way of object-condition.
An internal-object state is related to an external-object state by way of object-condition:
one reviews the external base of infinite consciousness; one reviews the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. An internal-object...

He reviews the divine eye externally; the divine ear-element …pe… the knowledge of the modes of psychic power …pe… the knowledge of recollecting past lives …pe… the knowledge of passing away and rebirth according to one’s kamma …pe… he reviews the knowledge of future states.
He contemplates with insight the external aggregates, which have internal objects, as impermanent, suffering, and non-self …pe… by means of the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds.

The mind of one possessing a mind that has an internal object and an external mind is known [by another]; external aggregates with an internal object are related to knowledge of the minds of others (cetopariya-ñāṇa),
knowledge of recollecting past lives (pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa), knowledge of the destiny according to deeds (yathākammūpaga-ñāṇa), knowledge of future states (anāgataṃsa-ñāṇa),
and advertence (āvajjanā) by way of object condition (ārammaṇapaccaya).
A state with an external object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with an external object:
one reviews an external divine eye; one reviews the divine ear-element.

[So too] the knowledge of supernormal power … the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds … the knowledge of recollection of past lives … the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma … the knowledge of future existences.

He reviews [them]. He contemplates external aggregates with an external object as impermanent, suffering, and non-self …pe… through the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds, he knows the mind of one possessing an external mind with an external object.

External aggregates with an external object are the object of the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of the destination according to deeds (*yathākammūpaga-ñāṇa*).
Knowledge of the future is related to advertence by way of object-condition.
An external state is related to an internal state by way of object-condition:
having given a gift, undertaken precepts, and performed the Uposatha duty, one reviews that; one reviews past deeds well done.

Having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna. Noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path, review the fruit, review the defilements abandoned regarding external objects, review the defilements suppressed, and know the defilements previously habitually practiced. An external object [is known] internally.

One reviews the divine eye, the divine ear-element, the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power, the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their karma, and the knowledge of future existences;

one contemplates with insight the internal aggregates as impermanent [and so forth] upon an external object; one relishes and delights in that, and taking that as an object, it becomes internally object-directed.

Lust arises … [and so on] … grief arises. Internal aggregates with external objects are related to the knowledge of supernormal powers (*iddhividha-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of recollecting past lives (*pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of the destination according to karma (*yathākammūpaga-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of future states (*anāgataṃsa-ñāṇa*), and to advertence (*āvajjanā*) by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).
Dominance (*adhipati*).
A state with an internal object is a condition for a state with an internal object by way of predominance-condition (adhipatipaccaya):
as object-predominance (ārammaṇādhipati) and as conascent-predominance (sahajātādhipati). As object-predominance: one esteems and reviews the internal base of infinite consciousness;
one esteems and reviews the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. [One esteems and reviews] the internal divine [eye].

Having treated the eye as important … pe … having treated the divine ear-element … pe … the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power … the knowledge of recollecting past lives … the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their karma … the knowledge of future states as important … pe … having treated internal aggregates with internal objects as important,
one relishes them and delights in them; having treated those as important, lust arises with an internal object.
A view arises. Conascence-predominance: internal-objective predominance is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for the associated aggregates.

An external-objective state is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for an external-objective state. Conascence-predominance: external-objective predominance is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for the associated aggregates.
An external object phenomenon is a condition for an internal object phenomenon by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). As objective predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*):
having given a gift, undertaken virtue, or performed the Uposatha duty, one esteems and reviews it;
one reviews former good deeds; having emerged from jhāna … [and so on] … the Noble Ones, having emerged from the Path, esteem and review the Path.

They review, making the fruit their object of esteem. They review, making the internal divine eye—which has an external object—its object of esteem … [and so on] … the divine ear-element … the knowledge of the modes of psychic power … the knowledge of penetration into others’ minds … the knowledge of recollection of past lives … the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds … the knowledge of future existences;
they review these, making them their objects of esteem, with an external object.
Having esteemed the internal aggregates, one relishes them and delights in them;
having esteemed them, lust with an internal object arises, and wrong view arises.
[This is] immediate.
A state with an internal object is a condition for a state with an internal object by way of proximity condition:
preceding aggregates with an internal object are a condition for succeeding aggregates with an internal object by way of proximity condition.
A state with an internal object is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for a state with an external object:
a death-consciousness with an internal object is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for a rebirth-linking consciousness with an external object;
a life-continuum with an internal object is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for an advertence with an external object. [States] with an internal object...
The aggregates are related to emergence with an external object by way of proximity condition. Adaptation with an internal object is related to change-of-lineage;
adaptation is related to purification; adaptation is related to the attainment of fruition; for one emerging from cessation;
and the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is related to the attainment of fruition by way of proximity condition.
A state with an external object is a condition, by way of proximity condition, for a state with an external object:
preceding aggregates with an external object are a condition, by way of proximity condition, for subsequent aggregates with an external object;
conformity with an external object is a condition for change-of-lineage; conformity is a condition for purification.

… the lineage (gotrabhū) is a condition for the path by way of proximity-condition; purification (vodāna) is a condition for the path by way of proximity-condition; the path is a condition for the fruit by way of proximity-condition; the fruit is a condition for the fruit by way of proximity-condition; conformity (anuloma) is a condition for the attainment of fruition (phalasamāpatti) by way of proximity-condition.
An external object-dhamma is a condition for an internal object-dhamma by way of proximity-condition—an external object-dhamma...
Life-continuum consciousness is a condition for a rebirth-linking consciousness with an internal object by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
Life-continuum with an external object is a condition for advertence with an internal object by way of proximity-condition.
Aggregates with an external object are a condition for emergence with an internal object by way of proximity-condition.

A state with an internal object is a condition, by way of proximity condition (*samanantara-paccaya*), for a state with an internal object … [and so on] … by way of co-nascence condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*) … by way of mutuality condition (*aññamañña-paccaya*) … by way of dependence condition (*nissaya-paccaya*).
Strong-dependence (*upanissaya*): … [and so on].

A state with an internal object is a condition for a state with an internal object by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)—namely, as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support ... [etc. ... Natural decisive support:

the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self with an internal object are conditions for the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and [the contemplation of non-self] with an internal object.
It is a condition for the contemplation of non-self by way of the decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

An internal object-dharma is a condition for an external object-dharma by way of the decisive support condition—namely, as immediate decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakati-upanissaya*) ...
[and so on] ... Natural decisive support: the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self with an internal object.

Contemplation of non-self is related to contemplation of impermanence, contemplation of suffering, and contemplation of non-self with an external object by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state with an external object is related to a state with an external object by way of decisive support condition— namely, as proximity-decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*).
Natural decisive support … [as above] … Natural decisive support: the contemplation of impermanence with an external object, the contemplation of suffering,

and the contemplation of non-self with an external object are related to the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self with an external object by way of decisive support condition.

An external object state is a condition for an internal object state by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, as object-decisive-support, proximity-decisive-support, and natural-decisive-support …pe…. As natural-decisive-support:
the contemplation of impermanence, suffering, and non-self with an external object is a condition for the contemplation of impermanence, suffering, and non-self with an internal object.
Contemplation of non-self is a condition for [the subsequent state] by way of the decisive-support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). As for the repetition condition (*āsevana-paccaya*):
a state with an internal object is a condition for a state with an internal object by way of the repetition condition—the preceding...
Preceding aggregates with internal objects are related to subsequent aggregates with internal objects by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).

A state with an internal object is related to a state with an external object by way of the condition of repetition: adaptation with an internal object is related to change-of-lineage by way of the condition of repetition; adaptation is related to purification by way of the condition of repetition.
A state with an external object is a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for a state with an external object:
preceding aggregates with an external object are a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for subsequent aggregates with an external object;
conformity with an external object is a condition for change-of-lineage; conformity is a condition for purification.
… the lineage (gotrabhū) is a condition for the path by way of repetition-condition; purification (vodāna) is a condition for the path by way of repetition-condition.
Kamma:
An internal-objective state is a condition for an internal-objective state by way of kamma-condition—namely, co-nascent [kamma].
[This is] asynchronous. Conascent volition with internal object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates.
At the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on]. Asynchronous volition with internal object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates with internal objects.

A state with an internal object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with an external object. As asynchronous: volition with an internal object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates with an external object.
A state with an external object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with an external object—both as co-nascent and as asynchronous. As co-nascent:
volition with an external object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for its associated aggregates.

Condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking … [as appropriate] … Asynchronous: volition with an external object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates with an external object.

An external-object phenomenon is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for an internal-object phenomenon. Asynchronous: volition with an external object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates with an internal object.

Resultant and other states having an internal object are related to a state with an internal object by way of the condition of result (vipāka-paccaya) … pe … by way of the condition of nutriment (āhāra-paccaya) … by way of the condition of faculty (indriya-paccaya) … by way of the condition of jhāna (jhāna-paccaya) … by way of the condition of path (magga-paccaya).
Condition … by way of association condition … by way of presence condition … by way of absence condition … by way of disappearance condition … by way of non-disappearance condition.
Section on Enumeration.

In the pure (suddha) condition: two by way of root-cause (hetu), four by way of object (ārammaṇa), three by way of predominance (adhipati), four by way of proximity (anantara), four by way of contiguity (samanantara),

two by way of co-nascence (sahajāta), two by way of mutuality (aññamañña), two by way of dependence (nissaya), four by way of strong-dependence (upanissaya), three by way of repetition (āsevana), [two] by way of kamma (kamma)...
Four [in the case of] resultant; two ... (two in all cases) ... two in association, two in presence, four in absence, four in disappearance, two in non-disappearance. (Thus it should be counted.
Positive.

The Negative Extraction (Paccanīyuddhāra): A state with an internal object is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a state with an internal object; it is a condition, by way of co-nascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*), for a state with an internal object; it is a condition, by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*), for a state with an internal object; it is a condition, by way of kamma-condition (*kammapaccaya*), for a state with an internal object.

A state with an internal object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with an external object; it is a condition, by way of decisive support-condition, for a state with an external object; it is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with an external object.
An external object phenomenon is a condition for an external object phenomenon by way of object-condition, conascence-condition, decisive-support-condition, and kamma-condition.
An external object phenomenon is a condition for an internal object phenomenon by way of object-condition, decisive-support-condition, and kamma-condition.
1.22.7.2. Negative Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya)
In the Enumeration Chapter,
regarding the pure [conditioning relations]: four for not-root, four for not-object, four for not-predominance, four for not-proximity (abbreviated).
In all cases, there are four [conditions] for not-prenascence, not-postnascence, not-repetition … pe … not-dissociation, four … pe … not-non-disappearance, four. (Thus it should be counted.
Negative.

1.22.7.3. Positive-Negative Conditionality (Paccayānulomapaccanīya) With root condition (hetupaccaya), there are two [answers] for non-object (na-ārammaṇa), two for non-predominance (na-adhipati), and two each for non-proximity (na-anantara), non-contiguity (na-samanantara), non-strong-dependence (na-upanissaya), non-repetition (na-āsevana), non-kamma …pe… non-absence (na-atthi), and non-disappearance (na-vigata). (In all cases there are two. Thus it should be counted.
This concludes the Positive-Negative Conditionality.
1.22.7.4. Negative-Positive (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma) With non-root condition (nahetupaccaya):

four in object (ārammaṇa), three in predominance (adhipati), four in proximity (anantara), four in contiguity (samanantara), two in conascence (sahajāta), mutuality (aññamañña), and support (nissaya), four in decisive support (upanissaya), three in repetition (āsevana), and four in kamma (kamma).

In the resultant [condition], two; ... pe ... in the associated [condition], two; in the presence [condition], two; in the absence [condition], four; in the disappearance [condition], four; in the non-disappearance [condition], two.
(Thus it should be counted. Negative-Positive.
The Section on Questions.
The Triplet on Internal Objects is finished.
